label: Between actual CONCRETE_6 individuals at w, what is PRIOR_4 to the other grounds it
paraphrase: OPEN analyst bridge, attribution deferred, the PRIOR_4 weak sibling of 86efed1a: at the selected world w, if y and x are both concrete and exist at w and y is prior to x in being (PRIOR_4: y can be without x and x cannot be without y, DEF-CAN-BE-WITHOUT), then y grounds x under the selected relation at w. It assumes that both relata are actual concreta, so an absent or non-concrete prior thing (the second falsifier recorded for 86efed1a; on the real-possibility reading of CanBeWithout every necessary abstract object would be PRIOR_4 to every contingent being it can be without) does not touch it, and it is stated for PRIOR_4, so the hand-and-stick case that falsifies 86efed1a on PRIOR_1 does not touch it either (the stick can be without the hand). Support option (this batch): it follows from c4bb0481 (what is PRIOR_4 to x is something x depends on for its being and which does not depend on x; claim 95f41960 reads In V Metaph. lect. 13 n. 18 as dependence running one way) and the distinct-relata bridge a8298fbd (an actual concretum's distinct actual dependee grounds it, also used in argument 57f22435); so it shares their dependencies and is not independent warrant beside them. ST I q.104 a.1 states the converse direction (per se preservation: the preserved cannot exist without the preserver, dependence to cannot-be-without), so it is not warrant for this bridge. Kept scope condition: a necessary condition that is no ground (a flame cannot be without oxygen, oxygen can be without the flame) satisfies PRIOR_4 among actual concreta; the bridge then needs the selected relation to count such conditions as grounds, which the principal-sustaining reading of the converse bridge 98efaa9e excludes. DEF-CAN-BE-WITHOUT fixes real possibility; whether real possibility is natural possibility or possibility by divine power (by which the flame could be without oxygen) is open, and decides whether such cases are PRIOR_4 at all.
